# YouTube fixtures

Scrubbed snapshots of youtube.com pages, served at the real origin in tests
so the content script injects exactly as in production.

**Naming:** `<type>-<anything>.html` where type is `home`, `watch`,
`subscriptions` or `shorts`. The e2e suite picks up every file matching that
pattern, so adding a capture is just dropping the file here.

**Synthetic fixtures** (`*-synthetic.html`) are generated by
`node tools/make-synthetic-fixtures.mjs` from YouTube's known element
structure. They are the stable baseline. Real captures catch what the
generator does not know about.

## Capturing a real page

1. Open youtube.com in Chrome, logged in, on the page you want: `/`,
   `/feed/subscriptions`, a `/watch?v=` page, or a `/shorts/` page. Scroll
   enough that at least 12 videos have loaded.
2. Open devtools, Console tab. Paste the whole contents of `tools/capture.js`
   and press Enter. A file named `youtube-<type>-<date>.html` downloads.
3. Open the download in a text editor and search for a channel name you know
   and a word from a real video title. Neither should be there. If anything
   real survived, do not commit it; report the text so the scrubber can be
   fixed.
4. Rename to `<type>-<date>.html` (for example `home-2026-10-06.html`), move
   it here, and run `npm test`.

Capture at least `home`, `watch` and `subscriptions`, ideally on two
different days so layout drift shows up in the suite.
